name: Umbrian dialect
notes: Umbrian dialect (modern Romance, NOT the ancient Italic language). Central Italian of Umbria. Transitional between Tuscan and Southern varieties. Key features: (1) No gorgia. (2) Some assimilatory processes (ND→nn, MB→mm) shared with Roman. (3) Partial metaphony in eastern Umbrian varieties (Rohlfs 1966, Loporcaro 2009). GRAPHEMES: the grapheme table and its positional readings come from it-IT through graphemes_base, because the variety writes standard Italian spelling. ⟨c g⟩ read [tʃ dʒ] before ⟨e i⟩ and [k ɡ] elsewhere: cielo [ˈtʃɛːlo], gelo [ˈdʒɛːlo] (Bertinetto & Loporcaro 2005, JIPA 35(2), p. 133). ⟨i u⟩ before a vowel are the glides [j w]: pieno [ˈpjɛːno], chiave [ˈkjaːve], guida [ˈɡwiːda] (p. 139, Table 2 on p. 138). The spec keeps its own ⟨s⟩ and ⟨z⟩ readings and does not take the it-IT positional ones: the it-IT intervocalic [z] and word-initial [dz] are the Standard Northern values, and no source for this variety was opened.

sources.author: Bertinetto, P.M. & Loporcaro, M.
sources.title: The sound pattern of Standard Italian, as compared with the varieties spoken in Florence, Milan and Rome
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Phonetic Association
sources.notes: JIPA 35(2). Illustration of Standard Italian; states the preconsonantal /s/ voicing agreement and documents the Tuscan/Northern split in intervocalic ⟨s⟩. Table 2 (p. 138) and p. 139 give the opening and closing diphthongs and the hiatus that the stress diphthongs list follows; p. 137 gives the two equal vowels in hiatus.
